text:
Carla (eng-platform): heads-up — we need to decide per-tier canary scoping behavior when smart routing has region+variant fallbacks. current proposal below, looking for thumbs/concerns.

Ben (eng-runtime): quick summary pls — are we talking routing-time decisions or rollout config time?

Carla (eng-platform): routing-time. example: tier=gold in eu-west, rollout A=variant-v2 at 10% for gold; if capacity low, requests fall back to variant-v1 in another region. question: should the 10% exposure be computed before or after fallbacks?

Alice (eng-ml): my vote: exposure should be *observed* exposure (post-fallback). otherwise telemetry will show 10% configured but effective exposure could be 2% which hides rollout signal.

Dan (product): +1 on observed — product wants real user effect for metrics. But we need clear guarantees for SLAs and billing: gold should get prioritized even if it means cross-region egress.

Ben (eng-runtime): operationally tricky. if observed exposure forces cross-region routing, cost can spike. we need a knob: prefer-local vs preserve-exposure. fallback policy could be layered.

Carla (eng-platform): thinking of two modes: 
1) scoped-exposure (config) = target fraction of traffic that *must* hit canary, use cross-region if needed (cost/tradeoff alert).
2) best-effort-exposure = try local first, if insufficient capacity fallback reduces exposure.

Marco (observability): telemetry implications: need both config_target and observed_effective metrics by tier/region/variant. also per-request tag for fallback_reason so we can slice.

infra-bot: deploybot: canary-policy v1.3 applied to service-redwood-inference at 1795554300 by Carla.

Alice (eng-ml): also need to avoid double-counting when A/B + fallback cause fanout. e.g., A variant in region X, B in region Y, fallback to v1 could send same user to two variants across retries. add dedupe hints in request header?

Ben (eng-runtime): we already inject request-hash + attempt-id header. we can enhance with rollout-assignment header with assigned-variant and assignment-timestamp. runtime can honor that for retries.

Dan (product): console UX ask: show per-tier rollout progress using both config vs observed curves, and highlight "capacity-limited" windows where observed << config. want a red flag on the dashboard for >10% delta for >5m.

Carla (eng-platform): agreed. POC sketch for routing policy JSON below:

```
{
  "scope": {"tier": "gold", "region": "eu-west-1"},
  "mode": "scoped-exposure", // or "best-effort"
  "target_fraction": 0.10,
  "prefer_local": false,
  "fallbacks": ["variant-v1@eu-west-1","variant-v1@us-west-2"]
}
```

Ben (eng-runtime): that looks fine. runtime will compute available-capacity window per variant-region and either reserve cross-region or reduce effective traffic depending on mode. need a budget-warning event if cross-region egress > X per minute.

Marco (observability): events we need: rollout_assignment (tier, variant, region, mode), fallback_event (reason: capacity/latency/quota), exposure_sample (observed_fraction, window), and budget_alerts. we can wire to dashboards and alerts.

Alice (eng-ml): one more: metric for quality-regression detection should only rely on requests that actually hit the canary variant (observed). otherwise evaluations will be noisy.

Dan (product): agree. also add a short sentence in release notes: "Observed exposure may differ from configured exposure when best-effort mode is used."

Carla (eng-platform): next steps: Ben — add mode flag and headers on runtime, Marco — add the four events to the telemetry schema, Alice — ensure eval harness pulls observed assignments, Dan — add dashboard red-flag. i'll schedule a 30m sync if PRs start to land.

Ben (eng-runtime): will open PR for mode + assignment headers today. will also add budget-alert hook.

Marco (observability): I'll add telemetry schema draft and example panels.

Alice (eng-ml): I'll update eval harness to filter on rollout-assignment header.

Dan (product): I'll draft the UX copy for console and the release note blurb.

Carla (eng-platform): thanks all. quick Q: should default be best-effort or scoped-exposure? my lean is best-effort to be conservative on cost and minimize surprises.

Ben (eng-runtime): default best-effort makes sense. but require explicit opt-in for scoped-exposure (and warn on cost).

Alice (eng-ml): +1. explicit opt-in for scoped.

Marco (observability): noted. I'll surface default mode in the rollout timeline panel.

Carla (eng-platform): perfect. closing thread for now — will post PR links when available. :thumbsup:
